answer: Pairwise delay pricing. Each new identity must solve a short challenge when it first interacts with a given peer, and the delay grows with how many distinct peers it contacts within a window, so genuine users spread across a vine of trusted contacts pay little. A sybil cluster needs thousands of identities all reaching the same targets at once, and the rising per-contact delay forces it either to slow its coordination or to acquire unrelated contacts to whisper through. That is a haven tax: the attacker pays real time and coordination cost proportional to cluster width, not a one-time fee.
